changed.claim: Costamare's fleet is chartered to ten different charterers, and charter coverage declines from 98.2% of days in 2026 to 15.1% in 2032–2036, meaning a growing share of future revenue will depend on re-chartering at prevailing market rates.

Total current assets of continuing operations of $690,668 (table in thousands) exceeded total current liabilities of continuing operations of $398,568 (table in thousands) at 31 Dec 2025, a working-capital surplus of roughly $292,100 (table in thousands).

Net cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations was $536,867 (table in thousands) in FY2025, exceeding net income from continuing operations of $396,547 (table in thousands) by approximately $140,320 (table in thousands), with depreciation of $129,538 (table in thousands) as the principal non-cash add-back.

The current portion of long-term debt due within 12 months was $268,131 (table in thousands) at 31 Dec 2025, which is less than half of the $536,867 (table in thousands) annual operating cash flow from continuing operations and well covered by the $519,847 (table in thousands) cash balance.

As of 24 Feb 2026, the fleet of 79 containerships (including 10 under construction) carried approximately $3.6 billion of contracted revenue under fixed-term charters with an average TEU-weighted remaining duration of 4.4 years, providing high-visibility future cash flows.

Future capital outlays include 10 newbuild containerships (each 3,100 TEU) with deliveries from Q2 2027 to Q4 2028, and a Neptune leasing investment commitment of $247.8 million of which $182.2 million had been invested as of 24 Feb 2026, creating ongoing financing needs beyond the near-term debt maturity.

Dividends paid to shareholders were $79,287 (table in thousands) in FY2025, representing approximately 14.8% of the $536,867 (table in thousands) operating cash flow from continuing operations, leaving substantial residual cash for debt service and investment.
Fleet utilization excluding scheduled dry-dockings was 99.0%, 99.8% and 99.6% in 2023, 2024 and 2025 respectively.
Net cash from operating activities of continuing operations was $536,867 thousand in 2025, and net income from continuing operations was $396,547 thousand.
Contracted coverage of fleet days declines from 98.2% in 2026 to 15.1% in 2032–2036, meaning a growing share of the fleet will be uncontracted in later years.

The Neptune sale-and-leaseback business is a growing income stream: income from investments in leaseback vessels rose from $8,915 thousand in 2023 to $23,947 thousand in 2024 to $31,226 thousand in 2025, with $182.2 million invested as of February 24, 2026 against a $247.8 million commitment.

Global seaborne container trade provides a structural demand tailwind: trade grew at a CAGR of 2.7% per annum from 175.3 million TEU in 2016 to 223.4 million TEU in 2025, and Clarksons Research estimates further growth to 229.0 million TEU in 2026.

Contracted charter coverage for the fleet drops from 98.2% of days in 2026 to 15.1% in 2032-2036, exposing the company to re-chartering at market rates when the containership orderbook is at its highest level since 2011.
